name: Service Monitor
author: Centrix HIS Helper Tools
summary: Uptime monitoring for the hospital's systems: HTTP(S), TCP, ping and DNS checks in groups, with certificate and domain expiry, incidents and a shareable status page.
description: Watch the services the hospital depends on (HIS web and APIs, JasperServer, HL7 listeners, PACS, databases, DNS) from one place. Each monitor is checked in the background on its own interval, with retries before it is marked down, and shows up, slow or down with its response time, uptime and a heartbeat bar of its latest checks. HTTPS and TLS certificates and public domain registrations are read too, with warnings before they expire. Status changes are kept as incidents. A view-only status page can be shared by link, without sign-in. Everything is stored in SQLite, so no Centrix database connection is needed.
features: Monitor types: HTTP(S) (status codes, keyword, redirects), TCP port, ping (ICMP) and DNS (record type, server, expected answer)
Groups with their own colour and order; groups collapse to a combined heartbeat bar
Heartbeat interval, retries and retry interval before a monitor is marked down, request timeout and a slow threshold
Service Health: overall status, key numbers, search and status filters, a heartbeat bar per monitor, uptime 24 h / 7 d and response times
Monitor detail: response-time chart (1 hour to 7 days), uptime, p95, incidents and the latest checks
Certificate expiry (HTTPS and TLS ports) and domain name expiry (RDAP), each with its own warning and critical days
Incidents: every status change with its duration, ongoing or resolved
Share: a public, view-only status page by link, with or without targets and error texts, groups expanded or collapsed
Reset statistics now or on a schedule (every N days at a set time), for all monitors, a group or one monitor
Backup and restore of monitors, groups and settings as a .json file (add to, or replace, the current monitors)
Import monitors and groups from an Uptime Kuma 1.x backup
Light, dark or device theme, full-screen mode for wall displays
Built for many monitors: hourly totals, cached reads and up to 32 checks at the same time
Role permissions: view, Manage services, Check now and Reset statistics; Settings and Share for administrators
requires: SQLite for the monitors and their check history (no MongoDB connection needed)
Network access from the server to the monitored hosts; the ping command for ping monitors
Internet access to rdap.org for domain name expiry (optional)

actions.description: Create, edit, pause and delete services and groups
Run a check of a service, or of all services, straight away
Clear the check history and incidents (uptime, response times, heartbeats) of monitors
